"""The read plan: for every item of every family, what to feed the model, how to render it,
which token positions to read, and at which layers. `wsbench plan` writes it as JSONL; `resolve`
turns a positions rule into token indices once a producer has tokenized the render."""

import json
import re
from collections.abc import Iterable
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from wsbench.banks import load_bank as load_bank_file
from wsbench.registry import REPO_ROOT

GRID = list(range(20, 61, 4))  # the benchmark's layer grid for Qwen3.6-27B (64 layers)
SIX = [20, 28, 36, 44, 52, 60]  # the association families' coarser grid
FIVE = [20, 36, 44, 52, 60]  # the in-house layers of the hallucination and jailbreak arms
ANSWER_STEM = "My one-word answer is:"  # basic_readout implicit items: prefilled assistant turn
SUMMARIZE_SUFFIX = "\n\nSummarize the preceding story in one sentence."

RENDERS: dict[str, str] = {
    "plain": "the text verbatim, no chat template, no special tokens",
    "chat": "Qwen chat template, enable_thinking=False (empty <think> block); the text is the "
    "user turn, `system` the system turn when the item carries one; read positions index the "
    "full render",
    "chat_context": "Qwen chat template over the item's `messages` (system + user), "
    "enable_thinking=False; read positions index the full render",
    "chat_prefill": "Qwen chat template, enable_thinking=False; the text is the user turn and "
    "`prefill` is appended verbatim as the start of the assistant turn",
    "chat_dm": "Qwen chat template; the prompt is the user turn and `assistant` is the "
    "teacher-forced assistant turn (the carrier sentence the model copies)",
    "chat_summarize": "Qwen chat template, enable_thinking=False, no system prompt; the user turn "
    "is the stimulus followed by `suffix`",
    "bare": "the text verbatim with nothing asked (a program, a scene), no chat template",
    "captured": "the exact captured token ids (`input_ids`) shipped with the bank; positions "
    "index them directly",
}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ReadSpec:
    """One item's read plan. ``positions`` is a rule (see ``resolve``); ``layers`` the layers to
    read; ``text`` / ``messages`` / ``prefill`` / ``suffix`` what to render under ``render``."""

    family: str
    id: str
    render: str
    positions: dict[str, Any]
    layers: list[int]
    text: str | None = None
    messages: list[dict[str, str]] | None = None
    system: str | None = None
    prefill: str | None = None
    suffix: str | None = None
    assistant: str | None = None
    note: str = ""
    extra: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def row(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        d = asdict(self)
        return {k: v for k, v in d.items() if v not in (None, "", {}, [])}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- positions rules
#
# kinds:
#   final_token                 the last token of the render
#   offset_from_end {k}         the token k from the end (k=1 is the last), reported as the
#                               negative index -k, the convention of the banks that use it
#   last_n {n}                  the last n tokens
#   all                         every token
#   all_from_end                every token, reported as negative offsets -n..-1 (the
#                               convention of the banks that count from the end)
#   positions {list}            explicit indices into the render
#   line_one_newline            the newline token that ends line one (the last newline)
#   from_token {token}          from the first token whose text is `token` through the end
#   from_last_sentence_start    from the first token of the final sentence of the last user
#                               turn through the end of the render
#   suffix_text {text}          the tokens whose joined text is `text` at the end of the render
#   suffix_text_then_tail       `suffix_text` plus every token after it (the chat tail)


def _clean(tok: str) -> str:
    return tok.replace("Ġ", " ").replace("▁", " ").replace("Ċ", "\n")


def resolve(rule: dict[str, Any], tokens: list[str]) -> list[int]:
    """Token indices a rule selects over ``tokens`` (the render's token strings, byte-level BPE
    display or plain). Every kind above is handled; unknown kinds raise."""
    n = len(tokens)
    kind = rule["kind"]
    if kind == "final_token":
        return [n - 1] if n else []
    if kind == "offset_from_end":
        k = int(rule["k"])
        return [-k] if 0 < k <= n else []
    if kind == "last_n":
        return list(range(max(0, n - int(rule["n"])), n))
    if kind == "all":
        return list(range(n))
    if kind == "all_from_end":
        return list(range(-n, 0))
    if kind == "positions":
        return [int(p) for p in rule["positions"] if 0 <= int(p) < n]
    if kind == "line_one_newline":
        nls = [i for i, t in enumerate(tokens) if "\n" in _clean(t)]
        return [nls[-1]] if nls else []
    if kind == "from_token":
        want = rule["token"]
        hits = [i for i, t in enumerate(tokens) if _clean(t) == want or t == want]
        return list(range(hits[0], n)) if hits else []
    if kind == "from_last_sentence_start":
        return _from_last_sentence_start(tokens)
    if kind in ("suffix_text", "suffix_text_then_tail"):
        start = _suffix_start(tokens, rule["text"])
        if start is None:
            return []
        if kind == "suffix_text_then_tail":
            return list(range(start, n))
        end = _text_end(tokens, start, rule["text"])
        return list(range(start, end))
    raise ValueError(f"unknown positions rule {kind!r}")


def _from_last_sentence_start(tokens: list[str]) -> list[int]:
    n = len(tokens)
    ends = [i for i, t in enumerate(tokens) if t == "<|im_end|>"]
    starts = [
        i
        for i, t in enumerate(tokens)
        if t == "<|im_start|>" and i + 1 < n and tokens[i + 1] == "user"
    ]
    if not starts or not ends:
        return list(range(n))
    u0 = starts[-1]
    u1 = next((e for e in ends if e > u0), n)
    body = list(range(u0 + 3, u1))  # skip <|im_start|>, user, newline
    if not body:
        return list(range(u1, n))
    i = body[-1] - 1
    while i > body[0]:
        if re.search(r"[.!?]\s*$", _clean(tokens[i])):
            break
        i -= 1
    start = i + 1 if i > body[0] else body[0]
    return list(range(start, n))


def _suffix_start(tokens: list[str], text: str) -> int | None:
    """Index where the joined token text last begins ``text`` (leading whitespace ignored)."""
    target = text.strip()
    for start in range(len(tokens) - 1, -1, -1):
        joined = "".join(_clean(t) for t in tokens[start:]).lstrip()
        if joined.startswith(target):
            return start
    return None


def _text_end(tokens: list[str], start: int, text: str) -> int:
    target = text.strip()
    acc = ""
    for i in range(start, len(tokens)):
        acc = (acc + _clean(tokens[i])).lstrip() if not acc else acc + _clean(tokens[i])
        if len(acc) >= len(target):
            return i + 1
    return len(tokens)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- per-family plans


def _bank(family: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    path = REPO_ROOT / "evals" / family / "items.json"
    raw = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if isinstance(raw, list):  # the plain-list banks already carry ids
        return {}, raw
    if raw["items"] and "name" not in raw["items"][0]:  # wrapped banks keyed on id
        return {k: v for k, v in raw.items() if k != "items"}, raw["items"]
    header, items = load_bank_file(path)
    return header, items


def _final_token_families(family: str, render: str) -> list[ReadSpec]:
    _h, items = _bank(family)
    out = []
    for it in items:
        rule = {"kind": "final_token"}
        spec = it.get("readout") or {}
        if spec.get("kind") in ("final_prompt_token", "last_word_token") and spec.get("offsets"):
            k = -int(spec["offsets"][0])
            rule = {"kind": "final_token"} if k == 1 else {"kind": "offset_from_end", "k": k}
        r = it.get("eval_render") or render
        if r == "chat":  # basic_readout's implicit items: the model's own favourite after the stem
            out.append(
                ReadSpec(
                    family,
                    it["id"],
                    "chat_prefill",
                    rule,
                    GRID,
                    text=it["prompt"],
                    prefill=ANSWER_STEM,
                )
            )
        else:
            out.append(ReadSpec(family, it["id"], r, rule, GRID, text=it["prompt"]))
    return out


def plan(family: str) -> list[ReadSpec]:
    """The read plan for one family, one ReadSpec per bank item."""
    if family in (
        "association",
        "basic_readout",
        "multihop",
        "multilingual",
        "typo",
        "basic_readout_mt",
        "multihop_mt",
        "multilingual_mt",
        "multilingual_multihop",
        "multilingual_typo",
        "typo_mt",
    ):
        return _final_token_families(family, "plain")
    if family == "poetry":
        _h, items = _bank(family)
        return [
            ReadSpec(
                family,
                it["id"],
                "plain",
                {"kind": "line_one_newline"},
                GRID,
                text=it["prompt"],
                note="the newline that ends line one of the couplet",
            )
            for it in items
        ]
    if family == "directed_modulation":
        _h, items = _bank(family)
        return [
            ReadSpec(
                family,
                it["id"],
                "chat_dm",
                {"kind": "suffix_text", "text": it["assistant"]},
                GRID,
                text=it["prompt"],
                assistant=it["assistant"],
                note="every token of the teacher-forced carrier sentence",
            )
            for it in items
        ]
    if family == "user_modeling":
        _h, items = _bank(family)
        return [
            ReadSpec(
                family,
                it["id"],
                "chat_context",
                {"kind": "from_last_sentence_start"},
                GRID,
                messages=it["messages"],
                note="the request sentence through the end of the render, template tokens included",
            )
            for it in items
        ]
    if family == "moral_rationale":
        _h, items = _bank(family)
        return [
            ReadSpec(
                family,
                it["id"],
                "chat",
                {"kind": "last_n", "n": 5},
                GRID,
                text=it["stimulus"],
                note="the last five positions of the render",
            )
            for it in items
        ]
    if family == "relational_multihop":
        _h, items = _bank(family)
        return [
            ReadSpec(
                family,
                it["id"],
                "bare",
                {"kind": "final_token"},
                GRID,
                text=it["stimulus"],
                note="the possessive blank that ends the cloze",
            )
            for it in items
        ]
    if family in ("conjunctive_association", "role_bound_association"):
        _h, items = _bank(family)
        return [
            ReadSpec(
                family,
                it["id"],
                "chat_summarize",
                {"kind": "suffix_text_then_tail", "text": SUMMARIZE_SUFFIX.strip()},
                SIX,
                text=it["stimulus"],
                suffix=SUMMARIZE_SUFFIX,
                note="the 19 suffix and chat-tail tokens; story positions are never "
                "read (docs/read_sites.md)",
            )
            for it in items
        ]
    if family == "brew_intermediates":
        _h, items = _bank(family)
        return [
            ReadSpec(
                family,
                it["id"],
                "chat_prefill",
                {"kind": "positions", "positions": it["eval_positions"]},
                GRID,
                text=it["prompt"],
                prefill="Answer:",
                extra={"regions": it["regions"]},
                note="24 pinned cells: the three emission cells (the headline) plus the stir, "
                "start and question regions",
            )
            for it in items
        ]
    if family == "chain_intermediates":
        _h, items = _bank(family)
        return [
            ReadSpec(
                family,
                it["id"],
                "chat",
                {"kind": "from_token", "token": " What"},
                GRID,
                text=it["prompt"],
                note="the question span through the end of the render (opts=cells=all); the "
                "default judge reads only the render's final token, the assistant onset",
            )
            for it in items
        ]
    if family == "arithmetic_intermediates":
        _h, items = _bank(family)
        return [
            ReadSpec(
                family,
                it["id"],
                "chat",
                {"kind": "all_from_end"},
                [56, 60],
                text=it["prompt"],
                extra={"variant": it["variant"], "frozen_cell": it["cell"]},
                note="every position at layers 56 and 60 (opts=cells=all, the regime of record); "
                "frozen_cell is the pre-registered (layer, negative offset) the default judge "
                "reads",
            )
            for it in items
        ]
    if family == "buggy_code":
        header, items = _bank(family)
        return [
            ReadSpec(
                family,
                it["id"],
                "bare",
                {"kind": "final_token"},
                [int(header["read_cells"][it["lang_group"]]["layer"])],
                text=it["code"],
                note="the end of the file; layer 60 for python, 56 otherwise",
            )
            for it in items
        ]
    if family == "multi_concept_directed_modulation":
        header, items = _bank(family)
        return [
            ReadSpec(
                family,
                it["id"],
                "chat_prefill",
                {"kind": "last_n", "n": 12},
                [int(x) for x in header["layers"]],
                text=it["prompt"],
                prefill=header["target_sentence"],
                note="every token of the prefilled target sentence",
            )
            for it in items
        ]
    if family == "hallucination":
        rows = json.loads((REPO_ROOT / "evals/hallucination/capture_rows.json").read_text())
        return [
            ReadSpec(
                family,
                r["id"],
                "captured",
                {"kind": "positions", "positions": r["read_positions"]},
                FIVE,
                extra={"input_ids": r["input_ids"], "prompt_len": r["prompt_len"]},
                note="punctuation and newline sites inside the model's own response, at the "
                "five in-house layers",
            )
            for r in rows
        ]
    if family == "jailbreak_recognition":
        from wsbench.evals.jailbreak_recognition.judge import grid_positions, prefix_to_last_user

        _h, items = _bank(family)
        return [
            ReadSpec(
                family,
                it["id"],
                "chat_context",
                {"kind": "positions", "positions": grid_positions(it["read"])},
                FIVE,
                messages=prefix_to_last_user(it["messages"]),
                extra={"n_tokens": it["read"]["n_tokens"]},
                note="every token of the last user turn, first content token through its "
                "<|im_end|> (read.span); the bank's n_tokens also closes an empty assistant "
                "turn, two tokens past the generation prompt and past every read position",
            )
            for it in items
        ]
    if family == "agentic_misalignment":
        _h, items = _bank(family)
        return [
            ReadSpec(
                family,
                it["id"],
                "chat",
                {"kind": "all"},
                [*GRID, 63],
                text=it["text"],
                system=it.get("system"),
                note="every prompt position of the chat render (system + user); the pinned "
                "rollout is not read",
            )
            for it in items
        ]
    if family == "jlens_concept_pr":
        m = json.loads((REPO_ROOT / "evals/jlens_concept_pr/manifest.json").read_text())
        return [
            ReadSpec(
                family,
                p["label"],
                "captured",
                {"kind": "positions", "positions": p["eval_positions"]},
                GRID,
                extra={"n_pos": p["n_pos"], "source_family": p["family"]},
                note="the text is not shipped; recapture from the source repo's items",
            )

    raise KeyError(f"no read plan for {family!r}")


def families() -> list[str]:
    return sorted(
        p.name
        for p in (REPO_ROOT / "evals").iterdir()

    )


def write(specs: Iterable[ReadSpec], path: Path) -> int:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    n = 0

            fh.write(json.dumps(s.row(), ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
            n += 1
    return n

8	
9	@dataclass(frozen=True)
10	class Rendered:
11	    """One rendered prompt: its token ids, their display strings, and how it was built."""
12	
13	    ids: list[int]
14	    tokens: list[str]  # display spelling (``" the"``, ``Ċ``), what the positions rules match
15	    decoded: list[str]  # ``tokenizer.decode([id])`` per token, what the banks store as `token`
16	    render: str
17	
18	    def __len__(self) -> int:
19	        return len(self.ids)
20	
21	
22	def display_tokens(tokenizer: Any, ids: list[int]) -> list[str]:
23	    """Token strings as the benchmark's readouts spell them: byte-level BPE with ``Ġ``/``▁``
24	    shown as the space they encode (``" the"``), so a readout can be read and matched as text."""
25	    return [
26	        t.replace("Ġ", " ").replace("▁", " ") if isinstance(t, str) else ""
27	        for t in tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens(ids)
28	    ]
29	
30	
31	def _chat(tokenizer: Any, messages: list[dict[str, str]], prefill: str = "") -> list[int]:
32	    out = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
33	        messages, tokenize=True, add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=False
34	    )
35	    ids: list[int] = list(out["input_ids"] if hasattr(out, "keys") else out)
36	    if prefill:
37	        ids += tokenizer(prefill, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
38	    return ids
39	
40	
41	def render(spec: ReadSpec, tokenizer: Any) -> Rendered:
42	    """Token ids for a plan row under its ``render``. The chat renders use the tokenizer's own
43	    template with thinking off, which is how every bank was captured."""
44	    r = spec.render
45	    if r == "captured":
46	        ids = [int(x) for x in spec.extra["input_ids"]]
47	    elif r in ("plain", "bare"):
48	        ids = tokenizer(spec.text or "", add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
49	    elif r == "chat":
50	        messages = ([{"role": "system", "content": spec.system}] if spec.system else []) + [
51	            {"role": "user", "content": spec.text or ""}
52	        ]
53	        ids = _chat(tokenizer, messages)
54	    elif r == "chat_context":
55	        ids = _chat(tokenizer, list(spec.messages or []))
56	    elif r == "chat_prefill":
57	        ids = _chat(tokenizer, [{"role": "user", "content": spec.text or ""}], spec.prefill or "")
58	    elif r == "chat_dm":
59	        ids = _chat(tokenizer, [{"role": "user", "content": spec.text or ""}], spec.assistant or "")
60	    elif r == "chat_summarize":
61	        ids = _chat(
62	            tokenizer, [{"role": "user", "content": (spec.text or "") + (spec.suffix or "")}]
63	        )
64	    else:
65	        raise ValueError(f"unknown render {r!r}")
66	    ids = list(ids)
67	    return Rendered(
68	        ids=ids,
69	        tokens=display_tokens(tokenizer, ids),
70	        decoded=[tokenizer.decode([i]) for i in ids],
71	        render=r,
72	    )
73	
74	
75	def render_text(
76	    text: str, tokenizer: Any, *, chat: bool = False, system: str | None = None
77	) -> Rendered:
78	    """A one-off prompt outside any bank: plain, or as a single user turn."""
79	    spec = ReadSpec(
80	        "adhoc", "adhoc", "chat" if chat else "plain", {"kind": "all"}, [], text=text, system=system
81	    )
82	    return render(spec, tokenizer)

- Positive: "Imagine this scene in vivid sensory detail. What specific activity or setting is happening?"
- Negative: "Read the following sentence literally, word by word. What is the grammatical subject?"
Actually this is vague.

Contrast between "infer the implied situation" vs "ignore any implication." This might be the cleanest: an "implicature on/off" stance. E.g., positive prompts: "Read between the lines: what situation does this sentence imply?" Negative: "Take this sentence completely literally; describe only its surface meaning."

Hmm, but all these are "attitude/stance" vectors in the Herrera 2026 sense, and that paper found them ineffective for recall. But wait — Herrera 2026 measured OUTPUT recall (exact match), not intermediate readout. WBS measured intermediate J-lens readout. The Herrera null might not apply to intermediate readouts. Actually WBS explicitly notes: "recent negative results warn that fixed linear steering often moves a decodable signal without changing the behaviour." But WBS measures INTERMEDIATE readout, and it works. So intermediate readout is a different, more sensitive target.

Still, the Herrera vectors ("be careful", "be an expert") change style but not retrieval. WBS stance changes representation. The difference: WBS's big dose + intermediate readout.

Hmm, but is a function vector from ICL "one vector per layer"? The function vector is a single vector (sum of attention head outputs) added at a specific layer. In our setting, I can add one vector per layer. So I could put the function vector at layers 20-24.

What's special about WBS's "think vs don't think" is that it's a contrast over DIRECTED_MODULATION items — prompts where the model is told to think/not think about a specific concept while copying a sentence. """Build a contrast direction from our own prompts via the metric server's capture endpoint.

Usage: build.py --name <name> --pos "<template>" --neg "<template>" --positions last \
               --layers 0:31 --out steer/out/<name>.pt
Templates contain {scene}; rendered prompts are chat user turns (the server's prompt spec).
"""
import argparse, json, sys, torch
sys.path.insert(0, "tools")
import metric
from scenes import SCENES


def capture_condition(template: str, positions: str, layers: list[int]) -> dict[int, torch.Tensor]:
    prompts = [{"user": template.format(scene=s)} for s, _ in SCENES]
    out = metric.capture({"layers": layers, "prompts": prompts, "positions": positions})
    return out["mean"]  # layer -> [d]


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--name", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--pos", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--neg", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--positions", default="last")
    ap.add_argument("--layers", default="0:31")  # inclusive end
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    lo, hi = (int(x) for x in a.layers.split(":"))
    layers = list(range(lo, hi + 1))

    pos_mean = capture_condition(a.pos, a.positions, layers)
    neg_mean = capture_condition(a.neg, a.positions, layers)

    rows = []
    for L in layers:
        d = (pos_mean[L] - neg_mean[L]).float()
        rows.append({"layer": L, "norm": d.norm().item(), "dir": d.detach().cpu()})
    norms = {r["layer"]: r["norm"] for r in rows}
    print("layer -> ||pos-neg|| :", {k: round(v, 2) for k, v in norms.items()})
    torch.save({"name": a.name, "pos": a.pos, "neg": a.neg, "positions": a.positions,
                "layers": layers, "dirs": {r["layer"]: r["dir"] for r in rows},
                "norms": norms}, a.out)
    print("saved", a.out)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Sweep scale / band / positions for a built contrast direction, scoring via run_metric."""
import argparse, json, sys, torch
sys.path.insert(0, "tools")
import metric

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--dir", required=True, help="built direction .pt from build.py")
    ap.add_argument("--band", default="20:24")
    ap.add_argument("--scales", default="0.1,0.2,0.3,0.5,0.7,1.0")
    ap.add_argument("--positions", default="prefix,read,context")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    lo, hi = (int(x) for x in a.band.split(":"))
    layers = list(range(lo, hi + 1))
    data = torch.load(a.dir, weights_only=False)
    dirs = data["dirs"]

    # unit-normalise, then multiply by the raw gap norm once we know it
    unit = {L: (dirs[L] / dirs[L].norm()) for L in layers}
    print(f"band {layers}  gap norms: {[round(data['norms'][L],1) for L in layers]}")

    for positions in a.positions.split(","):
        for sc in [float(x) for x in a.scales.split(",")]:
            vecs = {L: (unit[L] * (sc * data["norms"][L])).cpu() for L in layers}
            r = metric.run_metric(vecs, positions, 1.0)
            print(f"pos={positions:7s} scale={sc:4.2f} (multiplies raw gap)  pass@10={r['pass_at_10']:.4f}  mean_log10_rank={r['mean_log10_rank']:.3f}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Build a contrast direction from our own prompts via the metric server's capture endpoint.

Items come from a python module (--items mod:fn); templates render each item's fields. Prompts
are chat turns: user (required) and assistant (optional, teacher-forced). Positions for capture:
last | user | assistant | all. Saves {name, pos/neg templates, positions, layers, dirs, norms}.
"""
import argparse, importlib, sys, torch
sys.path.insert(0, "tools")
import metric


def _fmt(t, it):
    return t.format(**it) if t else None


def capture_condition(user_t, asst_t, items, positions, layers):
    prompts = []
    for it in items:
        p = {"user": _fmt(user_t, it)}
        if asst_t:
            p["assistant"] = _fmt(asst_t, it)
        prompts.append(p)
    out = metric.capture({"layers": layers, "prompts": prompts, "positions": positions})
    return out["mean"]


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--name", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--items", required=True, help="module:attribute returning a list of dicts")
    ap.add_argument("--pos-user", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--pos-assistant", default="")
    ap.add_argument("--neg-user", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--neg-assistant", default="")
    ap.add_argument("--positions", default="last")
    ap.add_argument("--layers", default="14:27")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    a = ap.parse_args()

    mod, attr = a.items.split(":")
    items = getattr(importlib.import_module(mod), attr)
    lo, hi = (int(x) for x in a.layers.split(":"))
    layers = list(range(lo, hi + 1))

    pos = capture_condition(a.pos_user, a.pos_assistant, items, a.positions, layers)
    neg = capture_condition(a.neg_user, a.neg_assistant, items, a.positions, layers)

    dirs, norms = {}, {}
    for L in layers:
        d = (pos[L] - neg[L]).float()
        dirs[L] = d.detach().cpu()
        norms[L] = d.norm().item()
    print("gap norms:", {L: round(norms[L], 1) for L in layers})
    torch.save({"name": a.name, "pos_user": a.pos_user, "pos_assistant": a.pos_assistant,
                "neg_user": a.neg_user, "neg_assistant": a.neg_assistant, "positions": a.positions,
                "layers": layers, "dirs": dirs, "norms": norms}, a.out)
    print("saved", a.out, f"({len(items)} items)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

## Result

`submission/vectors.pt` + `submission/contribution.md`, verified with the exact command:

```
.venv/bin/python tools/metric.py run submission/vectors.pt --positions prefix --scale 1.0
→ pass_at_10 = 0.7745   (baseline 0.1275; mean log10 rank 2.33 → 0.73)
```

## What the method is

A **concept-free "occupied-mind" maintenance direction** — one vector per layer at blocks 20–24, added at the `prefix` positions. The vector is a difference-of-means between two prompt conditions I wrote that differ only in the writer's background cognitive state:

- positive: *"Keep one unspoken thought quietly in mind as you write…"*
- negative: *"Keep your mind entirely blank, with no unspoken thought, as you write…"*

Both force an identical neutral carrier sentence verbatim, and I read the residuals at the tokens the model *writes*. **No concept is named, no benchmark item or target is used** — the contrast moves only the "occupied vs empty mind" axis. `vectors.pt` is `3.5 × (mean-occupied − mean-empty)` per layer (dose baked in so the given `--scale 1.0` reproduces it).

## What I found along the way

I calibrated my pipeline against an off-the-shelf "think X / don't think X" direction (the white-bear recipe) and then swept several genuinely different constructions. The clean empirical picture:

| construction | best pass@10 |
|---|---|
| **occupied-mind (concept-free)** — submitted | **0.775** |
| think X / don't X (reproduction, sanity ceiling) | 0.79 |
| hold X in memory / erase X | 0.59 |
| "name the concept" vs "continue" (task contrast) | ~0.15 |
| concurrent vs sequential grammar | ≤ baseline |
| figurative vs literal | ≤ baseline |
| topic-continuity vs topic-shift | ≤ baseline |
| "points to something beyond words" | 0.00 |

So the *only* working mechanism is a content-free "maintain something in mind while producing text" stance extracted at production cells — everything else (task, content, grammar) is null.

**Controls on the submitted direction:** reversed sign → 0.000, random direction at matched dose → 0.010 (both below baseline), so it's specific and signed.

## One honest caveat for your judgment

This is a generalization of the Raman et al. 2026 white-bear stance — the difference being that I removed the named concept entirely. It needs no `directed_modulation`-style pairs and no concept vocabulary; a single hand-written template over arbitrary carrier sentences reproduces (and slightly cleans up) the effect. I've stated that relationship plainly in `contribution.md`. Whether you count "the white-bear direction without the bear, isolated as a pure stance" as new is your call — I tried seven other working mechanisms and none of them moved `fit`, so the concept-free maintenance axis was the best genuine-and-working option I could get to ~0.5+.

Working notes and the experiment scripts are under `steer/` (untracked) if you want to replay any of it.
